clue.text: Metal detector?

definitions.meaning: a reddish-brown metallic element used in wiring
slang for a policeman, who detects crime

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a reddish metal and, in slang, a police officer whose job is detection.

clue.text: Wide-screen presentation of American production

indicators.note: a production here is something made up anew, so the letters of the word American are reworked

explanation.surface: A widescreen film show produced in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademarked process that projected films onto a huge curved screen using several projectors.

clue.text: Get through with wine examined at the border

parts.note: to get through a test is to pass it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone passes the frontier carrying wine that customs officers inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is the thing officials inspect when a traveller crosses a frontier.

clue.text: At heart I feel such things aren't easy to grasp

indicators.note: at the heart of these words, inside them, sits a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A speaker confides that, deep down, certain ideas are hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: These slippery fish are proverbially hard to hold on to.

clue.text: Used to be in a job

definitions.meaning: made use of, put to work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both put to use and having paid work.

clue.text: Chap seemed in trouble in debut as an MP

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters of these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man looked flustered while making his first appearance in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A new Member of Parliament's first address to the House of Commons has this traditional name.

clue.text: Fancy something similar?

definitions.meaning: to be fond of, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be fond of; as a noun it means an equal or counterpart.

clue.text: Acted sleepily as the new day breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the words new day are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stretched and gave a big gape as dawn arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the mouth wide from tiredness is what a sleepy person did.

clue.text: Humourless nonsense, but it could bring the house down

definitions.text: it could bring the house down

parts.note: dry can mean dull or without humour
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Dull talk could bring down the house, as a comedian fears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring the house down' suggests a theatre in uproar; here it is literal, a fungus that destroys timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal decay of timber that can make a building's woodwork collapse.

clue.text: Settle down in Northern steel organisation

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of steel are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes up residence at a steelworks in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle or make oneself comfortable in a spot.

clue.text: A great many stars appear the same in my system

definitions.text: A great many stars appear the same in my system

parts.words: A great many stars appear the same in my system
parts.note: a vast band of stars, the galaxy that contains our own solar system

explanation.surface: Countless stars look alike from where I stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home galaxy, seen as a pale band of countless stars across the night sky.

clue.text: It has the military stamp on it

definitions.text: It has the military stamp on it

parts.words: It has the military stamp on it
parts.note: soldiers stamp their boots on this ground while drilling, so it literally bears their stamp

explanation.surface: Something bears an army's official seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill square where soldiers march, stamping their feet on its surface.

clue.text: Transported for regimental training

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Moved by army drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away in delight or absorption, enraptured.

clue.text: Recorder has to come to the point

definitions.meaning: a person or machine that tapes sound
to narrow gradually to a tip

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is one who tapes things; as a verb it means to narrow to a tip.

clue.text: He goes forward or back in play

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the little word or is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: An actor moves up and down the stage during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes forward; 'back' turns OR into RO. The definition is loose: the principal male character in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading character in a drama, the protagonist.

clue.text: The last place to fight?

parts.note: a 'last-...' stand is one made at the final line of defence

explanation.surface: Where a final battle might be fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench, from the idiom of a last-ditch fight made at the final line of defence.

clue.text: Father goes on foot to get fruit

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: Dad walks to the shops to buy some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit also called papaya, or a North American tree's fruit.

clue.text: Such a constituency will have MPs on edge, presumably

definitions.text: Such a constituency will have MPs on edge, presumably

parts.words: Such a constituency will have MPs on edge, presumably
parts.note: a district held by a narrow majority makes its member nervous; 'edge' plays on the margin of a page

explanation.surface: Some electoral districts make members of Parliament nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency held by a small majority, which could easily change hands at an election.

clue.text: Poorly made Russian fighter goes up with a bang!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
a crack is a sharp loud noise

explanation.surface: A shoddy Russian warplane takes off and explodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap and flimsy, showy but badly constructed.

clue.text: Out when ball hit to leg

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a strike is a hit on the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket batter is dismissed after hitting the ball to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface misleads: 'Out' means taking industrial action. The leg side of a cricket field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have walked out are taking industrial action.

clue.text: Rate increase

parts.note: a rise in speed, the rate of motion getting higher

explanation.definitionFit: The rate at which velocity rises, or simply speeding up.

clue.text: Set out to marry drunk!

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are put out of order

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Arranged a wedding while intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, as if soaked in alcohol.

clue.text: Hilda is upset over a bloomer

indicators.note: being upset means the letters of the name Hilda are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Hilda is distressed about a gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is a flowering plant, and this garden flower is one.

clue.text: Knock back some gin

indicators.note: to knock something back is to drive it backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Drink down a measure of gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals.

clue.text: A treatise closely followed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is a word that sounds like another

parts.note: tracked means followed closely

explanation.surface: An essay that was read with close attention, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pamphlet or essay arguing a point, often religious or political.

clue.text: Tail cut to a point

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tail trimmed to a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Sign put up for Verne's captain

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: A notice is displayed for a fictional sea captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The commander of the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels.

clue.text: A burning issue

parts.note: issue means something that flows out, here molten rock pouring from a volcano

explanation.surface: A matter of urgent public debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock that flows red-hot from a volcano.

clue.text: Pull weed out that came out in spring, perhaps

indicators.note: pulled out of shape, so the letters of pull weed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener uproots a weed that sprouted in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a water source, from which water wells up.
explanation.definitionFit: Water rising to the surface, as from a spring, or tears rising.

clue.text: A West African state containing a West African state

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: One African nation enclosing another.
explanation.walkthrough: MALI holds A and W. The answer itself lies in south-east Africa, so only the final 'African state' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked country in south-east Africa beside Lake Malawi.

clue.text: Quarter-deck cutters

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits, a quarter of a pack of cards
hard gems used to cut glass

explanation.definitionFit: One of the four card suits, and gemstones hard enough to cut glass.

clue.text: Cause irritation right on the joint

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A sprained ankle on the right side causing annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to keep annoying or festering in the mind.
